topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course on cancer therapy and outlines its main learning outcomes.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles, mechanisms, and systemic limitations of conventional non-targeted cancer treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific molecular vulnerabilities and defective cellular control pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of targeted therapy resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogene-addicted kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and examine how tumors develop resistance and drug addiction to these therapies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore antibody-based therapeutics that target cell-surface proteins to directly eliminate cancer cells or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for immune surveillance and the therapeutic reactivation or engineering of T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Clinical trends, challenges, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overall clinical outcomes, therapeutic obstacles, and emerging paradigms shaping the future of cancer management.
